Multiple datasets were employed to identify Crohn's disease (CD)- and ulcerative colitis (UC)-associated targets.

The sensor surface indents under pressure and bulges prominently when retracted from sticky surfaces dynamically altering the Hall sensor-magnet distance.

title: Landau-like formalism for the thermal-runaway and filamentation instabilities in switching Mott devices
abstractExcerpt: Correlated oxides can switch to a low-resistance state when exposed to a voltage, making these insulator-to-metal transition materials promising candidates for memristor technology. Switching in materials such as VO2 occurs because of a thermal-runaway instability that leads to the abrupt formation of a hot current-carrying metallic filament within the insulator. We study, theoretically and experimentally, this bias-induced switching as a non-linear dynamics stability problem.

title: Coupled enzyme discovery, evolution and synthetic yeast chassis adaptation for microbial biopolymer valorisation

s2.tldr: This framework addresses a central bottleneck in converting microbial biodiversity by computational sequence repository mining into deployable biomanufacturing systems and establish laccases as tractable entry points for oxidative biopolymer conversion and provide a generalizable platform for engineering yeast systems for sustainable carbon valorisation.

abstractExcerpt: The valorisation of biological polymers requires microbial systems that can both access recalcitrant substrates and convert the resulting carbon into useful products. Although microbial genome and metagenome resources provide an expanding reservoir of candidate depolymerizing and modifying enzymes, most discovery workflows remain disconnected from enzyme optimisation and host adaptation. Here we present a coupled sequence-based enzyme discovery, enzyme evolution and synthetic yeast chassis adaptation strategy for microbial biopolymer valorisation.

title: First principles calculations of electric-field-driven topological phase transitions in silicene, germanene and stanene

abstractExcerpt: The emergence of two-dimensional topological materials, particularly the group-14 monolayers known as silicene, germanene, and stanene has opened promising pathways for next-generation nanoelectronics and spintronics. Their buckled honeycomb structure and strong spin-orbit coupling allow for bandgap engineering via a perpendicular electric field, leading to topological phase transitions (TPTs) from non-trivial to trivial insulating states.

title: Deciphering fibroblast and myeloid-cell states in keloids: an integrative analysis identifies ANKRD1 as a ferroptosis-related candidate gene
abstractExcerpt: BackgroundKeloids are fibroproliferative skin disorders characterized by persistent extracellular matrix deposition and limited treatment options. Ferroptosis has been implicated in fibrosis, but the molecular basis of ferroptosis-related changes in keloids remains unclear.MethodsFibroblast-derived bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE44270 and GSE145725) were integrated to identify differentially expressed ferroptosis-related genes.

s2.tldr: A redesigned RCSB Protein Data Bank RCSB.org Advanced Search capability that supports intuitive discovery of 3D structures through a unified interface that integrates annotation‐, sequence‐, and 3D structure‐based searches, and embeds an interactive 3D viewer.

abstractExcerpt: The Protein Data Bank (PDB), established in 1971, is the primary global, open-access archive for experimentally determined 3D macromolecular structures (proteins, RNA, DNA). The research-focused RCSB.org web-portal provides access to these data alongside more than one million machine-learning-predicted structure models, greatly expanding the available structural landscape. Rapid growth of both experimental and computational structures has increased the need for powerful yet accessible search tools that serve a broad and diverse scientific community.

title: Two barriers to benchmarking structure-based virtual screening against the AcrB efflux pump: a sample-size ceiling and an identifiability failure
abstractExcerpt: Background. The AcrAB-TolC system is the principal constitutive efflux pump of Escherichia coli and an attractive adjuvant target. Virtual screening campaigns against its distal binding pocket have been published without the retrospective validation standard elsewhere in the field. This study asked whether such a benchmark can be built from the published literature. Methods. Compounds reported as AcrB inhibitors were filtered against an independent reproducibility screen and assigned to a binding site by the strongest structural or mutational evidence available.

abstractExcerpt: Understanding the dehydration mechanism of hydrated salts remains fundamentally important in solid state chemistry, as their behavior affect fields ranging from heat storage to heritage conservation and pharmaceutical crystallization. s2.tldr: This study evaluates the state-of-the-art of machine learning-based methods for nanobody structure prediction and benchmarks various HADDOCK workflows to model their interaction with antigens using different input nanobody ensembles and information scenarios and proposes an ensemble docking pipeline that achieves high success rates.

abstractExcerpt: Nanobodies exhibit antigen-binding affinities of the same order as those of antibodies, which, along with their small size and unique structural characteristics, makes them well-suited for therapeutic and diagnostic applications. The lack of coevolutionary signals in nanobody-antigen complexes, together with the broad complementarity determining region 3 loop (CDR3) conformational space, poses a challenge for predicting the 3D structure of those complexes with computational modeling and artificial intelligence-based methods.

title: Graded revision lets autonomous campaigns update symbolic laws of SiGeC semiconductors from mixed-fidelity evidence
abstractExcerpt: Autonomous materials campaigns combine published measurements, simulations at several levels of theory and curated compilations whose errors are known in kind but not in size. A value off the current law may be an error, a measurement under a special condition, or a lead to missing physics, and an outlier filter discards all three alike. Machine unlearning removes data from neural networks by costly or approximate retraining, and provenance records locate data origins without identifying which conclusions to revise.

title: Deciphering the potential molecular links between ochratoxin A and colorectal cancer: an integrated computational toxicological and single-cell transcriptomic study
venue: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology
abstractExcerpt: BackgroundOchratoxin A (OTA), a common foodborne mycotoxin, is classified as a potential human carcinogen. However, the specific molecular mechanisms linking OTA exposure to colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis remain poorly understood.MethodsWe employed an integrative computational approach combining network toxicology, multi-cohort transcriptomic analysis, and machine learning to identify potential connections between OTA and CRC. Functional enrichment analysis was conducted to characterize the associated biological processes.

title: An Ab Initio-Kinetic Framework for Predicting Electrochemical Passivation of Materials
abstractExcerpt: Recent years have seen a strong push towards data-driven discovery of materials in many areas, from structural alloys to energy devices to quantum materials. However, many applications involve prolonged exposure to aqueous and/or acidic electrochemical conditions that can promote material degradation. Despite the critical role of stability in determining material performance, there is a lack of models that are capable of predicting a material’s corrosion-passivation behavior without relying on empirical parameters or fitting.

abstractExcerpt: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training datasets and have limited physical transparency.
